category_title: Friendly, talkative boys who struggle to focus during independent reading
minimal_context: The student is participating in a one-on-one reading conference during the 15 to 20 minutes of independent reading time with a self-selected text.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We have 15 to 20 minutes for independent reading now. Please take out your self-selected text and begin reading.

STUDENT: Hey! How's it going? I was just talking to my friends about what we're doing after school.

TUTOR: Let's focus on the book right now. Go ahead and start reading.

STUDENT: I don't really want to read right now. Doing this is just a chore.

TUTOR: Just try your best to read the next few pages.

STUDENT: This is boring. I can't focus on this, reading makes me sleepy.

options.A: Circulate to have a brief conversation with the student, recording the title and page number of their self-selected text on a roster.
options.B: Agree with the student that they are having a rough time focusing on their self-selected text during the conference.
options.C: Break the independent reading task down into smaller chunks so that the reading can be completed during the session.
options.D: Provide immediate instructional feedback, helping the student understand exactly what they should have done during the independent reading time.
